payload.comment: Prior-art brief is internally consistent and well-grounded. All seven ideas cite traceable quotes from their respective arXiv sources; the two quotes from arxiv_2309_13866v2 (GhostNet-VGG robustness ranking, temperature-scaling caveat) extend beyond the visible truncated source text but are plausible given the paper's stated scope (calibration of quantized networks on PathMNIST), so no action is required beyond normal verification at implementation time. The augmentation_model_quality idea draws a general model-quality inference from a quote whose immediate context is machine unlearning; the inference is reasonable but the direct textual support is narrower than the hypothesis states—acceptable for a hypothesis_to_validate item. The hflip_only_aug proposal uses a built-in primitive (hflip) and therefore does not require extension approval; the label-preservation rationale is sound. The compact_conv_token_transformer proposal is a coherent, non-executable architecture spec: 28×28×3 input matches the standard MedMNIST distribution; the conv-tokenizer arithmetic (28→14→7, 49 tokens of dim 128) is correct; 4 heads × head_dim 32 = 128 matches the token dimension; a rough parameter count (~350 K) is well within the stated <2 M budget; the training recipe (AdamW, cosine schedule, class-weighted CE, hflip-only augmentation, no test-set leakage) is consistent with the pipeline constraints. No deterministic findings are present. No issues block progression to the next stage.
llm_issues: augmentation_model_quality: the cited quote is scoped to unlearning quality, while the hypothesis generalises to overall model quality/robustness; the inference is plausible but the direct textual support is narrower than the claim.

ghostnet_vgg_robustness and temp_scaling_calibration: the specific ranking and temperature-scaling claims are not visible in the truncated source text; verify against the full paper before relying on them in downstream design decisions.
